statement: Define foreign exchange as FEMA, 1999 does, and describe how the foreign exchange market is organised and who takes part in it
Read exchange rate quotations: direct and indirect quotes, two-way (bid and offer) quotes, and cash, tom, spot and forward value dates
Work out customer (merchant) rates, forward rates and cross rates from interbank quotes
Explain the factors that determine exchange rates and how the exchange rate mechanism works
Describe how a bank's foreign exchange dealing room operates and is controlled
Identify the derivative products used in foreign exchange business and what each is used for
Apply the RBI and FEDAI guidelines that govern foreign exchange dealings
Explain what correspondent banking is, why banks need it, and which services depend on an account relationship
source_caveats: The FATF due-diligence statements for cross-border correspondent relationships are not used in items.

statement: Distinguish Nostro, Vostro, Loro and mirror accounts from the direction of the relationship, and reconcile a Nostro balance
Describe the electronic modes of transmission and payment systems used for cross-border and domestic funds transfer: SWIFT, CHIPS, Fedwire, CHAPS, TARGET, RTGS and NEFT
source_caveats: CHAPS settlement mode: courseware (net) and Bank of England (gross) disagree; taught as a flagged caution, not scored.

statement: Identify who is an NRI or PIO under FEMA and distinguish NRE, NRO, FCNR(B) and SNRR accounts by purpose, currency, deposit form, credits, debits and repatriability
source_caveats: Income-tax residency tests and RFC accounts for returning NRIs are not taught (no primary source checked).
Courseware and RBI differ on the NRE term and on where rent may be credited; no item tests those points.

statement: Apply the conditions for advances against non-resident deposits and for housing loans to NRIs
Describe the facilities available to NRIs for investing in India: shares and securities, funds, deposits, firms and immovable property
Distinguish capital account and current account transactions and explain how the Foreign Exchange Management Act treats each
Apply the Liberalised Remittance Scheme: who is eligible, the annual limit, frequency, documents and how family and proprietors are treated
Identify the remittances that are permitted and those that are prohibited under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
source_caveats: Travel limits follow the RBI FAQ of 28 November 2025; the courseware may state different figures.

statement: Apply the operational conditions for capital account remittances and for gifts and loans to non-resident relatives under the scheme
source_caveats: The Overseas Investment Rules are taken from a secondary reproduction (2022 text); the Regulations and Directions (forms and timelines) were not retrieved and are not taught.

statement: Work out tax collected at source on remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
source_caveats: The statute says 'exceeding ten lakh rupees' without stating that the rate applies to the excess only; the items compute on the excess and say so in each stem.
The additional rate where PAN or Aadhaar is missing and TCS on transfers to an NRO account are not taught.

statement: State the reporting and other remittance facilities for residents that accompany the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
source_caveats: The reporting Master Direction (No. 18/2015-16) was not retrieved in substance (its RBI page lists only update history); reporting is taught as far as the LRS Master Direction states it (FETERS). The courseware's daily XBRL reporting is not taught.

statement: Define a documentary letter of credit and identify each party to it and what it does
Apply the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) and the liabilities, responsibilities and rights of the parties
source_caveats: UCP 600 itself was not retrieved; articles are taught from the courseware.

statement: Distinguish the types of letter of credit: irrevocable, confirmed, transferable, red and green clause, sight, usance, deferred payment, negotiation, back-to-back, standby and revolving
Explain standby letters of credit and how they compare with guarantees
source_caveats: The Guarantees Regulations, 2026 do not mention standby letters of credit; the courseware's commercial standby safeguards for imports could not be verified and are withdrawn. ISP 98's articles are not taught (ICC publication not retrieved).

statement: Trace the flow of an export letter of credit and an import letter of credit from application to payment
source_caveats: The credit flow is taught from the courseware (UCP 600 itself was not retrieved). EDPMS and IDPMS are taught under unit 5 (batch BFM-A-U05-B007).

statement: Scrutinise documents under a credit, handle discrepancies, crystallise import bills and follow up bills
source_caveats: The substantive text of RBI's 16 January 2026 export-import directions (in force 1 October 2026) was not retrieved.

statement: Identify the risks in letter of credit transactions and the safeguards available to banks
Apply the Uniform Rules for Bank-to-Bank Reimbursements (URR 725)
source_caveats: URR 725's text was not retrieved; the 10-day and three-banking-day rules are taught as the courseware states them.

statement: Apply International Standard Banking Practice (ISBP 745) when examining documents
source_caveats: ISBP 745's own text was not retrieved; the courseware gives only its history and aims. The current edition is ISBP 821 (2023), which is mentioned but not taught.

statement: Apply the Incoterms 2020 rules to allocate cost, risk and delivery between buyer and seller
source_caveats: Incoterms 2020's rule texts were not retrieved; rule lists and allocations are taught from the trade administration page and the courseware matrix, which omits DAP.

statement: Distinguish the exchange control and trade control frameworks that govern exports and imports, and the roles of RBI, DGFT, FEDAI and ICC
Apply the export declaration, documentation, time limit and payment rules for exporters
source_caveats: Export Regulations text is the RBI page with its footnotes; the January 2026 export and import directions (in force 1 October 2026, after the cut-off) are not taught; the Master Direction paragraph on rupee settlement was substituted on 17 July 2026 and only the account mechanics are taught.

statement: Apply the facilities connected with exports: agency commission, reduction in invoice value, claims, refund, extension of time, write-off and foreign currency accounts
source_caveats: The FEDAI effective date of realisation is taught under FEDAI Rules (batch BFM-A-U01-B009), not repeated here.

statement: Explain export finance: pre-shipment and post-shipment credit, and the Gold Card scheme for exporters
source_caveats: The page of RBI's Credit Facilities Directions saved is the version of 1 October 2026; earlier versions of Chapter XV were not retrieved.
Time-limited Trade Relief Measures directions are not taught; the Normal Transit Period and crystallisation come from FEDAI Rules (batch BFM-A-U01-B009).

statement: Describe the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System and the follow-up of export bills
Explain factoring and forfaiting and when each is used
source_caveats: The courseware gives LIBOR-based discount examples; the rules taught here come from the RBI Master Direction.

statement: Apply the exchange and trade control guidelines for importers, including advance remittance, time limits and evidence of import
source_caveats: The January 2026 import directions, in force from 1 October 2026, are not taught.

statement: Explain import finance and the Import Data Processing and Monitoring System
Distinguish supplier's credit from buyer's credit and describe the rules on trade credit
source_caveats: Trade credit figures come from the 2018 Regulations page as updated 16 February 2026; not re-checked against a consolidated 2026 text.

statement: Apply the guidelines to a case on export finance
source_caveats: The case uses assumed bank terms and a stated normal transit period; the period is from FEDAI Rules (batch BFM-A-U01-B009).

statement: Identify who may borrow and lend under the external commercial borrowing framework, the currency and forms of borrowing, and the borrowing limit
source_caveats: The courseware describes the earlier framework; if the examination follows it, older figures may be tested and are not taught.

statement: Apply the rules on maturity, cost of borrowing and end-use restrictions for external commercial borrowings
source_caveats: The maturity computation annex was not read; the trade credit spread is not tested because the regulation text and the courseware differ.

statement: Apply the operational rules for external commercial borrowings: receipt of proceeds, security, refinancing, change of terms and debt servicing
source_caveats: The Master Direction on ECBs, Trade Credits and Structured Obligations was not retrieved.

statement: Meet the reporting requirements for external commercial borrowings and explain conversion of a borrowing into equity
Apply the operational rules for foreign investment: transfers, pledge of shares and reporting
Explain foreign direct investment and foreign portfolio investment: key concepts, eligible investors and investees, instruments and prohibited sectors
Classify the risks in international trade and the ways to manage them
Apply the Reserve Bank guidelines on country risk exposure and the ECGC country risk classification
source_caveats: Country risk provisioning percentages (in the 2025 Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions) are not taught; the RBI Concentration Risk Management Directions copy is updated to 1 October 2026, after the cut-off.

statement: Explain the origin, role and regulatory position of ECGC and the principle of risk sharing
Describe the ECGC policies for exporters and what they cover and exclude
source_caveats: Only the Shipment Comprehensive Risks sheet was read from ECGC; other policy terms (small exporter limit, protracted default period, percentages) are from the courseware, which predates current ECGC literature.

statement: Describe the ECGC covers for banks, the guarantees and special schemes, and the obligations and claims procedure
source_caveats: Cover percentages, premiums and claim periods for bank covers are from the courseware; the ECIB sales literature could not be read as text and those figures are not tested.

statement: Describe the role, functions and products of EXIM Bank
source_caveats: EXIM Bank content is from the courseware only; no EXIM Bank or Government document was read.

statement: Explain the Reserve Bank's powers under FEMA over authorised dealers and the returns they file
source_caveats: The list of returns is from the courseware and was not checked against the Reserve Bank's current list.

statement: Explain the objective and legal character of FEMA and apply the Current Account Transactions Rules
source_caveats: The Current Account Transactions Rules copy is updated only to 26 May 2015; later amendments were not searched for. The courseware's account of ODI, RFC and RFC(D) accounts is not taught here.

statement: Describe the formation and functions of FEDAI
Explain ADRs, GDRs, FCCBs and FCEBs
source_caveats: ADR and GDR content is general market description from the courseware; the Depository Receipts Scheme was not read. The courseware's FCCB and FCEB conditions belong to the earlier framework and are not taught.

statement: Explain what an international financial services centre is and why GIFT City was set up
source_caveats: GIFT City start date, company counts and the tax exemption are the courseware's statements; the SEZ Act and Income-tax provisions were not read.

statement: Describe the role of the International Financial Services Centres Authority
Apply the licensing and capital requirements for a banking unit in an IFSC
source_caveats: The Regulations text is the consolidation as amended up to 14 July 2023; later amendments were not searched for. The courseware says licensing needs Reserve Bank permission; the Regulations name the IFSCA.

statement: Apply the prudential requirements for an IFSC banking unit
source_caveats: The IFSCA directions on reserve ratios, exposure norms and the specified liquidity ratios were not retrieved; the courseware's 3 per cent reserve ratio and 5/10 per cent exposure ceilings are not tested as current.

statement: State the business an IFSC banking unit may and may not do, and the relaxations for foreign portfolio investors
source_caveats: FPI tax relaxations at GIFT City are the courseware's account and were not checked against the Income-tax Act.

statement: Trace the evolution of technology in banking and weigh its benefits and limits
source_caveats: Content is the courseware's account; no external source was read.

statement: Describe the digital platforms used in international banking and the Reserve Bank monitoring systems
source_caveats: EDPMS and IDPMS mechanics and the eBRC date are checked against the Reserve Bank Master Directions; the courseware's EDPMS and FIRMS dates were not verified.

statement: Explain how fintech, artificial intelligence, big data and robotic process automation are used
source_caveats: Content is the courseware's account; dated fintech statistics are not taught.

statement: Explain how blockchain changes a documentary credit and its advantages
source_caveats: The blockchain credit flow is the courseware's illustrative description.

statement: State the challenges of fintech and blockchain and the developments in India
source_caveats: Statements about Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd and IDRBT's phased adoption are the courseware's and were not verified.
